definitions.explanation: A constraint on how much time is allowed for an activity, stay, or process. Commonly applied to dining, parking, exams, and various services.

examples.japanese: この{試験|しけん}には{時間制限|じかんせいげん}がある。
examples.english: This exam has a time limit.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べ{放題|ほうだい}は90{分|ぷん}の{時間制限|じかんせいげん}です。
examples.english: The all-you-can-eat has a 90-minute time limit.

examples.japanese: {時間制限|じかんせいげん}がないと、だらだらと{仕事|しごと}をしてしまいがちだ。
examples.english: Without a time limit, people tend to work in a lazy, drawn-out way.

notes:
Composed of {時間|じかん} (time) and {制限|せいげん} (limit, restriction). A very practical term encountered frequently in everyday Japanese life.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時間制限|じかんせいげん}がある / ない — there is / is no time limit
- {時間制限|じかんせいげん}を{設|もう}ける — to set a time limit
- {時間制限|じかんせいげん}{付|つ}き — with a time limit
- {時間制限|じかんせいげん}{内|ない}に — within the time limit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {制限時間|せいげんじかん} — time limit (same meaning, reversed word order; more commonly used for exams and competitions)
- {期限|きげん} — deadline, expiration date (for submissions, payments, products)
- {締|し}め{切|き}り — deadline (especially for work submissions)

NOTE ON WORD ORDER:
{時間制限|じかんせいげん} and {制限時間|せいげんじかん} are often interchangeable, but {制限時間|せいげんじかん} tends to emphasize the specific allotted time ("the allotted time is 60 minutes"), while {時間制限|じかんせいげん} emphasizes the existence of the restriction itself ("there is a time limit").
